title: Area
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Official outcomes a to f are tested; g (use IT) and h (recognise use) are not questions. π is 22/7 as in the families. The area of a circle (a) was met in Grade 7; Grade 8 adds how area grows with the radius and shapes made of circles and rectangles (rings, arched windows). A sector (b) is θ/360 of the circle. Surface area (c to e) is the total area of the faces, with open and closed containers and real jobs (painting a room, a label on a tin, a tent). Irregular shapes (f) are estimated on a grid with part squares as halves, and on a scaled grid each square stands for an area. Teacher to confirm: whether painting the four walls and ceiling of a room (one family) is the usual Kenyan textbook form.

skills.key_step: The child says the radius is used twice in the area, so the area grows by the square of the change in radius.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a circle.
floor.question: Radius 7 m (π = 22/7)

steps: For a scale change, square the factor.

board.do: Draw two circles, radius 7 and radius 14.
Point at the bigger circle.
board.say: Its radius is twice as long. Twice the area, or more?

board.do: Wait for the child to predict.
The child works out both areas: 154 and 616.

misconceptions.ask: Is the bigger pond only wider, or also longer?
Which formula has the 2?
How many lengths does an area use?
Inside or round the edge?
Is 14 the radius?

checks.question: Area of a circle of radius 21 cm?
A radius is made 3 times as long. How many times the area?

skills.key_step: The child names each part of the shape and its radius before calculating, and decides whether to add or subtract.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a circle.
floor.question: Radius 14 m

representations: a garden with a path drawn
contexts: a path round a school garden

board.do: Draw a garden of radius 7 m with a path 7 m wide round it.
Point at the outer edge.
board.say: What is the radius out to here?

board.do: Wait for 14 m.
The child shades the ring and writes big minus small.

misconceptions.ask: Does the radius cross the whole path twice?
Where does the outer radius start?
Is the path a circle or a ring?
Is the garden part of the path?
How much of a circle sits on top?
What about the top?
Is the width across the half circle a radius?

checks.question: A pond of radius 7 m has a path 3.5 m wide round it. Area of the path?
A window 28 cm wide and 40 cm tall with a half circle on top. Area?

skills.key_step: The child writes θ/360 and multiplies it by the area of the whole circle.

floor.prerequisite: Finds a fraction of a number.
floor.question: 1/4 of 616

representations: a paper circle cut into slices
steps: Find the area of the whole circle.
Check: less than the whole circle.

board.do: Draw a circle of radius 14 m with a 90° sector shaded.
Point at the shaded part.
board.say: What fraction of the circle is it?

board.do: Wait for 1/4.
The child finds 1/4 of 616.

misconceptions.ask: Does the sprinkler turn all the way?
Is 22 a length or an area?
How many times is r used in an area?
How many degrees in a full turn?
Is 60° half a turn?
Is the whole 100 degrees?

checks.question: Area of a sector of radius 21 cm and angle 120°?
A sector of 45° is what fraction of the circle?

skills.key_step: The child divides the sector area by the whole circle's area and then multiplies by 360.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a circle.
floor.question: Radius 14 m

representations: the lit part of a compound
steps: Find the area of the whole circle.
Divide the sector area by it.
contexts: a floodlight at the school gate

board.do: Draw a circle of radius 14 m with an unknown sector lit.
Point at the whole circle.
Wait for 616.
Write 154/616 = ? and ask what fraction that is.

misconceptions.ask: Is that the lit part or the dark part?
Is 0.25 an angle?
What is the area of the whole circle?
Is the area the angle?

checks.question: A sector of radius 7 m has an area of 77 m². Angle?
A sector of radius 21 cm has an area of 231 cm². Angle?

skills.key_step: The child names the three different faces and doubles each because every face has a twin opposite.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a rectangle.
floor.question: 5 cm by 4 cm

representations: a cardboard box opened into a net
contexts: cartons in a factory in Thika

board.do: Draw a box 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
Point at the front face.
board.say: Is there another face just like it?

board.do: Wait for the child to say the back.
The child lists the three pairs of faces.

misconceptions.ask: How many faces does the box have?
Does card fill the box or cover it?
What about the top and bottom?
Is adding lengths an area?

checks.question: Surface area of a box 6 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm?
Surface area of a cube of edge 4 cm?

skills.key_step: The child lists exactly which faces are covered in the story before adding any areas.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the surface area of a cuboid.
floor.question: 2 by 3 by 4

representations: a list of surfaces to paint
steps: Divide by what one litre covers.
contexts: a wooden box with no lid

board.do: Draw a classroom 8 m by 6 m by 3 m with a door and windows.
Point at the long wall.
board.say: What is the area of this wall?

board.do: Wait for 24 m².
The child lists all four walls and the ceiling.

misconceptions.ask: Is that a wall or the floor?
How many walls?
Is 8 + 6 an area?
Do we paint the windows?
Should the windows add paint?
How many 10s in 120?

checks.question: A room 5 m by 4 m by 3 m: four walls and the ceiling, less 6 m² of openings. Area to paint?
An open box 10 cm by 8 cm by 5 cm (no lid). Card?

skills.key_step: The child unrolls the curved side into a rectangle as long as the circumference, then adds the circles the story has.
representations: a label peeled off a tin
steps: Use the radius, not the diameter.

board.do: Draw a tin and its label unrolled into a rectangle.
Point at the long side of the rectangle.
Wait for the child to say the circumference.
The child adds the circles for a closed tin.

misconceptions.ask: Does the tank have a lid?
What is the water sitting on?
Is that the metal or the water?
Is 7 the radius?
Does the label cover the top?
How long is the label?
A closed tin has what at the ends?
Is there a lid too?

checks.question: A closed tin of radius 7 cm and height 20 cm. Metal?
A label on a tin 14 cm across and 10 cm tall?

skills.key_step: The child counts five faces (two triangles, three rectangles) and uses the straight-up height for each triangle.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a triangle.
floor.question: Base 3 cm, height 4 cm

representations: a tent or a Toblerone box
steps: Two triangles: ½ × base × height each.
Leave out a face only if the story says so.
contexts: a card box for a prize

board.do: Draw the net of a prism with 3-4-5 cm triangles and length 10 cm.
Point at the triangles.
board.say: How many, and what is each area?

board.do: Wait for two of 6 cm².
The child labels the three rectangles.

misconceptions.ask: Is the floor sewn in?
What closes the two ends?
Which measure goes straight up?
How many ends?
Is a triangle half a rectangle?
How many sides has the triangle?

checks.question: A prism with right-angled ends of 6, 8 and 10 cm, length 12 cm. Total surface area?
A tent: ends 4 m wide and 1.5 m high, sloping sides 2.5 m, length 5 m, floor sewn in. Cloth?

skills.key_step: The child counts whole squares and part squares in two separate tallies, then adds half the parts.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the area of a square.
floor.question: Side 5 m

representations: a leaf traced on squared paper
tallies of whole and part squares
steps: Add half the parts to the wholes.
Multiply by the area of one square if the grid has a scale.
contexts: a leaf from the school compound
an irregular shamba on a plan

board.do: Draw a leaf on a grid.
The child ticks whole squares and dots part squares.
Count the ticks and dots with the child.
Ask how much the dots are worth, and wait.

misconceptions.ask: Is a part square a whole one?
Do the part squares cover any of the leaf?
Where are the whole squares?
Is the area of a square its sides added?
How much ground does one square stand for?

checks.question: A leaf covers 34 whole and 12 part squares of 1 cm². Area?
A plot covers 18 whole and 6 part squares; each square is 10 m by 10 m. Area?
